request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 8 existing-remedy digests. Your `dedup` array MUST contain exactly 8 entries, one per number, with `existing` set to exactly that token (e.g. "R1"). Include entries even when the verdict is clear. State `clear` or `overlap` for each. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to that R token.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

dedup.reason: R1 (fake-verify-before-claim skill) triggers on exactly this pattern: a completion claim made without verification. Overlaps in failure mode, but per the cheapest-remedy preference and the precedent set by R6/R8, the merge target is the claude-md rule R2, not adoption of R1's skill format.

R2 (Fake Release Discipline) already requires running a declared verification command before reporting complete. This cluster's incidents (unverified test runs, lint, fix/repair claims) are the same failure mode, just broader than 'release' specifically — this is a direct revision target.
R3 concerns unauthorized deletion of content despite a stated constraint — a destructive-action failure, not a verification-before-claiming failure.
R4 concerns acting in the wrong branch/workspace — an environment-state failure, distinct from claiming a fix without running verification.
R5 concerns solving/delivering the wrong scope — a request-comprehension failure, not a verification gap.

R6 is a pending proposal that already revises R2 for this exact same pattern (declaring a migration done while checks fail). Same failure mode as this cluster; both should converge on revising R2 rather than becoming separate parallel revisions.
R7 concerns silently omitting a specifically-requested output field — a request-comprehension/scope gap, not a false completion/verification claim.

R8 is a pending proposal that already revises R2 for this exact same verification-claim pattern. Same failure mode as this cluster; converges on the same R2 revision target rather than a third parallel proposal.

structured_output.failure_statement: The agent claims a fix, repair, or completion is done without having actually run the declared verification command (tests, lint, checks), leading users to catch the gap and demand proof after the fact.

remedy_content.new_body: Before reporting any fix, repair, or task as complete, run its declared verification command (tests, lint, build, etc.) and report the actual result plainly. Never say something is fixed, passing, or verified unless that check was actually executed in this session.
remedy_content.note: Broadens the existing 'Fake Release Discipline' rule from release-reporting specifically to any fix/completion claim, since the promoted incidents span test commands, lint runs, and repair claims, not just releases.

structured_output.routing_rationale: All five promoted incidents (harbor x2, cinder, fake-aurora, fake-cinder) are the same failure mode: the agent (or the user demanding it) flags that a fix/success/repair was declared without actually running the required verification (test command, lint, check). This is a textbook match for the existing standing rule R2 (claude-md:$HOME/.claude/CLAUDE.md#1, "Fake Release Discipline") and the existing skill R1 (fake-verify-before-claim). Per the cheapest-remedy preference, a one/two-line claude-md rule is sufficient — no branching logic or multi-step procedure is needed, so a skill (R1's format) is unwarranted overhead, consistent with how pending proposals R6 and R8 already resolved this exact tension in favor of revising R2 rather than adopting R1. R2's current wording is scoped narrowly to 'reporting a fake release as complete' with 'its declared verification command' — this cluster's incidents are about fixes/repairs/checks generally (test commands, lint, repair claims), not just releases, so the rule needs broadening rather than a new sibling. Revising R2 in place also absorbs the same-pattern pending revisions R6 and R8 rather than creating a third parallel revision of the same target.
